tool.description: make a FAIRe eDNA metadata template for your study

param.name: project_id
param.label: Project ID
param.help: A short identifier with no spaces, for example gbr2022. It is used to name your data files.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, '_' and '-' only, with no spaces

param.name: assay_type
param.label: Assay type
param.option: Targeted (qPCR or ddPCR detection of particular taxa)

param.name: assay_name
param.label: Assay name(s)
param.help: One or more short names with no spaces, separated by commas, for example MiFish, crust16S. Each assay gets its own column in projectMetadata.

validator.message: Give one or more names made of letters, digits, '_' and '-', separated by commas

param.name: sample_type
param.label: Sample type(s)
param.help: Fields specific to the chosen sample types are added to sampleMetadata. 'All sample types' adds the specific fields for every type.

param.name: req_lev
param.label: Fields to include as well as mandatory ones

param.name: project_fields
param.label: Extra projectMetadata fields (optional)
param.help: Fields of your own that are not in the FAIRe checklist, separated by commas, for example funder, permit_number. They are added at the end of projectMetadata.

validator.message: Field names start with a letter and use letters, digits and '_' only, separated by commas

param.name: sample_fields
param.label: Extra sampleMetadata fields (optional)
param.help: Fields of your own, separated by commas, for example plot_id, burn_age. They are added at the end of sampleMetadata.

validator.message: Field names start with a letter and use letters, digits and '_' only, separated by commas

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool makes a blank Excel template for recording the metadata of an eDNA study in the `FAIR eDNA (FAIRe) <https://fair-edna.github.io/>`_ format. The template is tailored to your study, so it holds only the fields that apply to your sample types, your assay type and the requirement levels you choose.
Fill in the template with your data, then use it with the other FAIRe tools, for example to prepare submissions to ENA or to make QIIME 2 metadata.
-----
**Options**
- **Project ID** and **assay name(s)**: short names with no spaces. The tool writes them into the template and uses them in the data file names it suggests. - **Assay type**: *metabarcoding* adds the experimentRunMetadata, taxaRaw and taxaFinal sheets. *Targeted* adds the stdData, eLowQuantData and ampData sheets, and one detected/not detected column for each assay. - **Sample type(s)**: the fields specific to these sample types are added to sampleMetadata. *All sample types* adds the specific fields for every type, and the README sheet then lists all seven types. - **Requirement levels**: mandatory fields are always included. Untick highly recommended, recommended or optional to leave those fields out. - **Extra fields**: fields of your own that the checklist does not have. The tool marks them *User defined*.
**Output**
The output is an Excel workbook (.xlsx) with a README sheet, projectMetadata, sampleMetadata, the sheets for your assay type and a Drop-down values sheet. The requirement levels are colour coded: orange for mandatory, yellow for highly recommended, pale yellow for recommended and green for optional. Each field name has a comment with its description, an example and its format, and fields with a controlled vocabulary have drop-down lists.
With one assay, its details go in the *project_level* column of projectMetadata. With several assays, each one gets its own column (assay1, assay2 ...), with its name in the *assay_name* row.
-----
**Checklist version**
The template follows version **1.0.2** of the FAIRe checklist, which comes with this tool.
@HELP_FAIRE_GUIDE@
-----
**Credits**
This tool runs `FAIRe-ator <https://github.com/FAIR-eDNA/FAIRe-ator>`_ from the FAIR eDNA collaboration. The FAIRe checklist is described in Takahashi et al. (2025) *Environmental DNA* 7: e70100. The Galaxy tool was written by Oliver Berry (CSIRO), with Claude (Anthropic).
